prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics, physics, and electrotechnics.

learning_outcomes.text: The student is knowledgeable about the behavior of single-stage amplifiers, Cascode amplifier, differential amplifier over a wide frequency range.
The student is knowledgeable about the operation of feedback circuits.
The student is knowledgeable about the behavior and dimensioning of digital integrated circuits in ratio logic and CMOS logic.
The student is knowledgeable about the behavior of complex digital circuits such as decouplers, multiplexers, decoders, ROM and RAM memories.
The student is knowledgeable about the main scaling techniques proposed in the literature.
The student is able to analyze various advanced analog circuits in bipolar technology with particular emphasis on design choices.
The student is able to analyze, dimension, and draw on wafer all integrated digital circuits in MOS logic, with the support of circuit simulations using SPICE software and Microwind2 layout editor.
The student acquires autonomous judgment skills, which is an essential prerequisite for creative design activities that fall within the capabilities of applying knowledge.
Students are stimulated to acquire tools that allow for independent study of the topics covered.
Learning verification methodologies tend to develop students' communication skills.

syllabus_topics: Analog Electronics: Overview of bipolar junction transistor (BJT) operation.
Low/high frequency response of common emitter BJT amplifier and frequency response; SPICE simulations.
Cascode configuration: medium/high frequency analysis; SPICE simulations.
Differential amplifier; medium/high frequency behavior and SPICE simulations.
Introduction to Digital Electronics: Overview of semiconductor physics.
Figure of merit for a digital system.
Transfer characteristic of an inverter and notable voltages.
Realization of a diode and a resistor.
Analysis of enhancement N-channel MOSFET operation.
Ratio Logics: Resistive load NMOS inverter and problems.
Overview of EE, ED NMOS inverters.
Evaluation of exact and approximate propagation time.
Design and dimensioning using arc graph theory and Euler paths.
Scaling Techniques: Constant field, voltage, and frequency scaling techniques.
Complex Circuits in CMOS Logic: Decoupling stages (buffers), transmission gates, multiplexers, decoders in pseudo-NMOS NOR logic.
Minimum access time if ROM is square.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written and an oral test, and a discussion of project work and/or exercises.
